findings.title: Webhook secret compared with plain !== and no method check
findings.body: The secret comparison is not constant-time, so timing can leak it. If the header is absent and the env var is unset, `undefined !== undefined` is false and the check passes. The constant guards this, but the check should be explicit. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers, and reject when the header is missing or not a string. Also restrict the handler to POST.

findings.title: Computed keys from z.string().toString() make a nonsense schema
findings.body: `z.string().toString()` returns "[object Object]" (or similar), so the schema just requires a property of that literal name. With sync enabled, every response fails validation and throws "Invalid refreshed tokens". Use `z.object({access_token: z.string()}).passthrough()`, or `.catchall(z.unknown())`.

findings.title: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a safeParse result, not the key
findings.body: `key` becomes `{success, data}` and is saved to the credential. That corrupts the Google credential. Use `.data` after checking success. The earlier `googleCredentialSchema.parse` also validated the credentials and threw on failure.

findings.title: Unconditional token refresh on every client creation
findings.body: `getClient` now refreshes the token on every call, ignoring expiry and the sync option. It does not use refreshOAuthTokens. `prisma` is not imported in this file. `statusText !== "OK"` is fragile, for example on HTTP/2. It also makes an extra network call per instantiation. Use refreshOAuthTokens, and only refresh when needed.

findings.title: Unhandled zod parse and JSON.parse/decrypt errors
findings.body: `parse` throws on a bad body, and `JSON.parse` and `symmetricDecrypt` throw on bad payloads or a wrong key. These become unhandled 500s instead of 400s. Use `safeParse` and wrap decrypt and parse in try/catch to return 400.

findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token injected for every provider
findings.body: If a response has no refresh_token, the literal "refresh_token" is written in. This applies to the non-sync path too. Zoom and Office365 schemas then store a bogus refresh token that breaks later refreshes. Only do this in sync mode, or keep the existing token.

findings.title: Sync endpoint returns a raw fetch Response with no auth or error handling
findings.body: Callers expect provider-specific shapes. Google reads `res.data` and Hubspot reads `.expiresIn` on the result, but this returns a fetch Response. That breaks those callers, and Zoho and Bigin read `.data.error`. The request also has no auth or secret header and does not check `response.ok`. Normalize the result per caller and authenticate the request.

findings.title: credentialId passed where userId is expected
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` takes a userId, but the credential id is passed. With sync enabled, the sync endpoint would be asked for the wrong user's credentials. Pass the credential's userId.

findings.title: Unrelated change of redirectUri to hardcoded slug
findings.body: The change replaces `appConfig.slug` with a literal and is unrelated to the credential sync request. Revert it.

findings.title: Flag is a string, not a boolean
findings.body: `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` evaluates to a string or undefined, not a boolean. Wrap it in `Boolean(...)`.
